facts.text: A practical validation argument can allocate different evidence sources to four questions: correct perception, correct software decisions, safe execution by the real machine, and whether the complete intervention improves rather than degrades real operations.
facts.quote: A practical validation argument can be organised around four questions, each served by different evidence sources

facts.text: Applying the same evidence source to all four validation questions—perception, software decisions, real-machine execution, and operational improvement—is a central validation mistake.
facts.quote: the central mistake would be to apply the same source to all four.

facts.text: Evidence sources for determining whether the system perceived correctly include field replay, sensor simulation, targeted real environment, shadow mode, and statistical sampling.
facts.quote: | Did the system perceive correctly? | Field replay, sensor simulation, targeted real environment, shadow mode, statistical sampling |

facts.text: Evidence sources for determining whether the software made the right decision include software-in-the-loop (SIL), closed-loop simulation, formal and requirements-based tests, replay where appropriate, and rare-event generation.
facts.quote: | Did the software make the right decision? | SIL, closed-loop simulation, formal and requirements-based tests, replay where appropriate, rare-event generation |

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) provides evidence about command, timing, and interface behaviour when assessing whether the real machine executed a decision safely.
facts.quote: HIL for command, timing and interface behaviour

facts.text: Controlled whole-machine tests provide evidence about stopping, traction, and dynamics when assessing whether the real machine executed a decision safely.
facts.quote: controlled whole-machine tests for stopping, traction and dynamics

facts.text: Evidence sources for determining whether the complete intervention improves rather than degrades real operations include operator simulation, nuisance-intervention testing, shadow operation, staged deployment, and operational monitoring.
facts.quote: | Does the complete intervention improve rather than degrade real operations? | Operator simulation, nuisance-intervention testing, shadow operation, staged deployment, operational monitoring |
